title: Convention Center Funding and Progress Push
summary:
*   **Convention Center Development Moves Forward:** Over $100,000 was approved to secure legal and appraisal services for land acquisition, preparing the way for the new Convention Center project.
*   **Market Study Funding Debated:** A proposal for an additional $25,000 to update the Convention Center's economic impact analysis faced opposition, passing its initial vote with one "no" due to cost concerns.
*   **New Committee Formed for Convention Center:** A special committee, chaired by the Mayor, was established to accelerate the project's timeline and provide further reports by mid-May.

Mayor Cooke called to order the special called meeting of the Council, noting the absence
of Councilmembers Urdy and Nofziger. CONVENTION CENTER Council had before them for
consideration an ordinance transferring $174,500.00 from the Convention Center Reserve
Fund to the Convention Center CIP Fund for the services of David Armbrust with the law
firm of Armbrust & Brown for legal/real estate services, W.F. Smith for appraisal
services, and Coopers & Lybrand for updating the Market, Financial, and Economic Impact
Analysis in connection with the Convention Center Project. After discussion the following
motions were made:
Motion
Councilmember Carl-Mitchell made a motion, seconded by Mayor Cooke to retain W.F. Smith
Co. to do the appraisal footprint for $73,000.00; retain David Armbrust to do the legal
and real estate work on each one of the individual parcels, representing the City, not to
exceed $30,000; and proceed with Coopers and Lybrand with their proposal and ask the City
Manager to continue to work with them to see if we can negotiate any parts of the price of
the total package as it deals with trying to be very prudent and what numbers are needed
prior to the bond election.
Councilmember Humphrey asked what the hourly rate is for Coopers & Lybrand and was told it
is $180.00 an hour. City Manager Barnett said she wanted to clarify that all amounts are
not to exceed those specified "if we can bring it in lower we certainly will".
Councilmember Carl-Mitchell suggested they divide the question because both Councilmembers
Humphrey and Barnstone had expressed reservations about spending the money for an updated
market analysis.
Mayor Cooke said, "We have the motion and we will divide all three parts". Results are as
follows.
Motion
The Council, on Councilmember Carl-Mitchell's motion, Mayor Cooke's second, waived the
requirement for three readings and finally passed an ordinance approving W.F. Smith for
appraisal services and transferral of $73,000 from the Convention Center Reserve Fund to
the Convention Center CIP Fund to do the appraisal footprint. (5-0 Vote, Councilmembers
Urdy and Barnstone absent.) Council Memo

CONVENTION CENTER
Council held a worksession after being given a Status Report on Convention Center Project.
They discussed the timeline and Mayor Cooke said he wanted a committee to meet several
times before May 15, 1989. Mayor Cooke said he would chair the committee and appointed
Councilmembers Barnstone and Carl-Mitchell as members.
The first meeting was set for April 28, 1989. PERSONNEL SUMMIT
